problem: Consider a plane lamina of mass $0.8\,\text{kg}$ and center of mass $(3,1),$ where $x$ and $y$ are measured in meters. If the moment of inertia of the lamina about an axis perpendicular to the lamina passing through its center of mass is $2\,\text{kg}\cdot {\text{m}}^{2},$ what is the moment of inertia of the lamina about an axis parallel to the first passing through the point $(1,-1)?$
worked_solution:
For a plane lamina of mass $M$ and a line ${l}_{M}$ perpendicular to the lamina passing through its center of mass, the parallel axis theorem states that the moment of inertia of the lamina about a line $l$ parallel to ${l}_{M}$ is given by

$$
{I}_{l}={I}_{M}+{d}^{2}M,
$$

where $d$ is the distance between the lines, and ${I}_{M}$ and ${I}_{l}$ are the moments of inertia about the lines ${l}_{M}$ and $l,$ respectively.

The distance between the line through the center of mass $(3,1)$ and the line through the point $(1,-1)$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}d & =\sqrt{(3-1)^{2}+(1-(-1))^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{4+4} \\  & =\sqrt{8} \\  & =2\sqrt{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Then, applying the parallel axis theorem, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{I}_{l} & =2+(2\sqrt{2})^{2}\cdot 0.8 \\  & =2+6.4 \\  & =8.4.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the moment of inertia is $8.4\,kg\cdot {m}^{2}.$
